Definition: from G4862 and a derivative of a compound of the base of 3674 and the base of G3725; to border together, i.e. adjoin:--join hard.
BiblicalUsage: Paul departs from the synagogue and enters into a certain man's house, named Justus, one that worships God, whose house joins hard to the synagogue. The house next door to the synagogue becomes the new meeting place, and the gospel moves one wall over when the old room shuts its doors.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God has a house next door whenever the synagogue shuts its doors, and I hold that Justus's house shows me the gospel is never left homeless.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
